_comment: Self-hosting dev pack -- WRITE-ENABLED slice. Lets jichi WRITE, but fenced
hard and under the autonomy envelope. Run with --auto (unattended) + budgets,
on a BRANCH, never master. See docs/proposals/2026-08-self-hosting-dev-pack.md.
editScope = tests/**, docs/**, CHANGELOG.md  -- a POSITIVE allow-list: the
edit tools CANNOT touch src/ or include/, so the loop cannot modify core
code OR its own guardrails (the envelope, the path fence). This slice
writes tests and docs only; src/ edits are a later, more careful slice.
verify = make test  -- a red verify rolls back to the last green checkpoint
(fix-forward verifyRetries times first). Override --verify 'make smoke' for
smoke drivers, or 'make check-target'/'make ci' for the full gate.
revertOutOfScope = true  -- a stray src/ change made via the SHELL (which
editScope does not fence) is detected and reverted to the run-start tree.
selfReview, snapshots, pathFence, privilegedCommands=deny  -- the usual wall.
learnOnStop = true  -- a clean run drafts lessons (docs/LEARNING.md).
_editscope_comment: M517 -- TIGHTENED, and the rule is stated so the next widening is a
decision rather than a slip: THE FENCE MAY ADMIT ONLY FILES THAT THE
VERIFY RUNS, OR THAT CANNOT AFFECT A GATE.
It used to be tests/** + docs/** + CHANGELOG.md against verify 'make
test', and that was inconsistent in two ways that a review run found:
- tests/** admits all 231 smoke drivers, and `make test` runs the UNIT
suite only -- so a weakened lint passed its own verify trivially, and
revertOutOfScope could not help because tests/ was IN scope.
- docs/** admits the 74 graded assignment test.sh graders (plus the
trace capturers), which no verify command here runs either. Weakening
a grader is how a learner gets failed for a correct answer -- see
M511, which fixed 24 real defects in exactly those files.
So the list below names the files the pack's two write commands actually
need: /add-test writes a unit test (covered by `make test`), /update-docs
writes the ROADMAP, an analysis page and the CHANGELOG (prose, which
cannot weaken a gate).
TO AUTHOR A GATE (a smoke driver, an e2e rig, an assignment grader) the
operator passes BOTH flags, deliberately, per run:
--edit-scope 'tests/smoke/*.sh' --verify 'make smoke'
Two explicit flags for a deliberate act; the unsafe combination is not
reachable by default. Widening one without the other is the defect this
comment exists to prevent.
_instructions_comment: M516: task rules, loaded on top of the root CLAUDE.md. A review
session needs a rubric that a general session does not, and the
rules block is capped at 32 KB -- so per-task files, not one
